newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico sees slow change on bank deposit guarantees.
newsitem.headline: Mexico sees slow change on bank deposit guarantees.

text.p: Mexico's top banking official on Friday said the government would move carefully in lowering bank deposit guarantees, and also sounded a note of caution on bank mergers.

Eduardo Fernandez, head of the Mexican Banking and Securities Commission, said the government's guarantee of all deposits was necessary during the 1994-96 banking crisis, but that it was also flawed and needed changing.
Earlier, Finance Minister Guillermo Ortiz said the deposit guarantees would be gradually reduced beginning in 1998, though small savers would continue to be fully protected.

"Despite the necessity (of change), it is important to wait a certain amount of time until the indicators in the banking system show conditions of undeniable health, so that the reduction of coverage doesn't generate undesirable effects of deposit concentration," Fernandez said in a speech at the annual Mexican Bankers Association convention.
In his speech, he also said he expected to see more mergers in the banking system during the next few years, cutting the number of banks while bolstering competition.
Foreign banks have swooped into Mexico in the wake of the crisis, buying up Mexican institutions at bargain prices to keep them from undercapitalization and collapse.

Fernandez welcomed the move, but said some checks may need to be applied to avoid monopolies. "To guarantee the healthy development of the system over the long term, we must be careful that the process of consolidation does not lead to an excessive concentration," he said.
